content.text:
This Outlook Scheduling Assistant screenshot shows six attendees (Priya Shah, Elena Ruiz, Jamal Wright, Sofia Moreno, Tom Becker, Marcus Lee) and the room NYC-09 Battery (6) on Wednesday. I need a 60-minute meeting with all six attendees in that room, within 9:00-17:00, starting on a quarter hour. Treat busy, tentative (hatched) and out-of-office blocks all as busy. Exactly one of these existing meetings may be moved to another day: Design review, Vendor call, or 1:1 Priya / Tom (moving a meeting frees that time for everyone who attends it; nothing else changes). Which single move creates the earliest possible start for the new meeting? Answer with the meeting name exactly as written above.

Think step by step. Then end your reply with one final line in exactly this form:
FINAL ANSWER: <your answer>

message.content:
**Step 1: Map busy time (including tentative) within 9:00-17:00**

- **Priya:** 9:30-10:15 (1:1), 10:45-11:45 (Release check), 14:15-15:00 (tentative Sprint planning), 16:45-17:45
- **Elena:** 10:00-11:00 (unlabeled blocks), 11:45-12:45 (Design review), 12:45-13:15 (tentative), 14:30-15:00 (Standup), 17:00-17:30
- **Jamal:** 9:00-10:30 (Training and a block), 10:30-11:00, 11:45-12:45 (Design review), 13:30-14:15 (Vendor call), 14:30-15:15 (Data sync)
- **Sofia:** 9:15-9:45, 10:15-11:45 (QBR prep), 13:30-14:15 (Vendor call), 14:15-15:00 (Partner call), 16:45-17:30
- **Tom:** 9:30-10:15 (1:1), 11:00-11:30 (Retro), 14:30-15:00, 15:00-15:30 (Retro), 17:00-18:00
- **Marcus:** 9:15-9:45, 10:15-10:45, 11:00-11:30, 11:45-12:45 (Design review), 14:30-15:30 (Staff meeting), 16:45-17:30 (tentative)
- **NYC-09 Battery:** 9:30-10:30 (Recruiting), 12:45-13:15 (Exec staff), 15:00-15:30 (Recruiting), 16:45-17:30 (Town hall prep)

**Step 2: Find the current earliest slot**

Sofia's QBR prep (10:15-11:45) blocks every start from 10:15 to 11:45. The room is busy 9:30-10:30 and Elena is busy 10:00-11:00, so nothing opens before 11:45 without a move. Without any move, the first free 60-minute window is 15:30-16:45.

**Step 3: Evaluate each allowed move**

- **Design review (11:45-12:45; Elena, Jamal, Marcus):** Freeing this block leaves 11:45-12:45 open for everyone. Priya and Sofia are free from 11:45, Elena's next block is the tentative one at 12:45, and the room is free until its 12:45 Exec staff block. Earliest start: **11:45**.
- **Vendor call (13:30-14:15; Jamal, Sofia):** This opens 13:15-14:15 once Elena's tentative block and the room's Exec staff block end at 13:15. Earliest start: **13:15**.
- **1:1 Priya / Tom (9:30-10:15; Priya, Tom):** The room is still busy 9:30-10:30, and Sofia blocks 10:15-11:45 anyway. The earliest start stays after 11:45, and the design review block then pushes it later.

**Step 4: Compare**

Design review gives 11:45, which is earlier than the 13:15 from moving Vendor call. No move can produce a start before 11:45, because Sofia's QBR prep and the room's 9:30-10:30 booking are fixed.

FINAL ANSWER: Design review

I'm checking Marcus's calendar against the hour markers: a busy block at 8:15–8:45, others at 9:15–9:45 and 11:00–11:30, an interview at 10:15–10:45, and a staff meeting from 14:30 to 15:30. I'm also placing his tentative block at 16:45–17:30 and starting on the exec staff room booking.

I'm checking the remaining busy blocks against the hour markers, then listing each person's busy spans together to look for a free hour inside the 9:00 to 17:00 window that works for all six calendars and the room.

The only open hour for all six calendars and the room is 15:30 to 16:45, since the room's recruiting slot ends at 15:30.

I'm ruling out the short gaps and settling on 15:30 to 16:45 as the earliest free hour for everyone. I'm also starting to consider whether moving one of the existing meetings could open up an earlier slot.

I'm checking the remaining candidate slots against each calendar, looking at whether moving the design review or the vendor call would open something earlier than 15:30. I'm also testing whether the 1:1 between Priya and Tom could shift to free up the morning.

I'm weighing whether moving the design review would open something earlier, and it would free 11:45–12:45 for Elena, Jamal, and Marcus. I'm checking the other blockers around that window: Sofia and Priya are busy until 11:45, while Elena and Jamal look open from 11:00 to 11:45.

I'm checking whether anything earlier than 11:45 works if the design review moves, and I'm looking at Elena's 11:00 to 11:45 gap to see if it could open a slot sooner.

I'm checking whether moving the vendor call would open an earlier slot: Jamal and Sofia would be free from 13:30, and I'm testing whether a window starting at 13:15 works once Elena's block ends.

I'm checking whether moving the vendor call opens something earlier than 11:45: Sofia's calendar is free from 11:45 until her partner call at 14:15, Elena's tentative block ends at 13:15, and the room opens up at the same point, so 13:15 to 14:15 looks clear for everyone.

I'm testing whether moving the Priya–Tom one-on-one would free anything earlier, since its 9:30–10:15 slot is the only block left in the morning that could shift.

I'm checking whether moving the Priya–Tom one-on-one would open anything: their 9:30–10:15 slot shares the room with Recruiting, so the room stays blocked until 10:30. Even then, Sofia is busy until 11:45 and the design review holds 11:45–12:45, so this move doesn't beat 11:45.

I'm checking whether moving the design review frees anything before 11:45, and Sofia's QBR prep, running 10:15 to 11:45, blocks any hour-long window that starts before then. The design review moved gives 11:45, and the vendor call moved gives 13:15.

I'm settling on design review at 11:45 as the earliest start, since Sofia's QBR prep blocks anything before that, and the vendor call move only gets me to 13:15.

I'm checking the 9:15 start: the room is busy from 9:30, so that doesn't work either. Sofia's QBR prep blocks everything from 10:15 to 11:45, and nothing can move that, so the design review moved to give an 11:45 start is the earliest option.
